content: The information provided is extensive and highly detailed, primarily focusing on drug interactions involving various medications and their effects on hepatic and intestinal enzyme metabolism, particularly CYP3A4. 1. Lenacapavir and CYP3A4 Substrates: Initiating CYP3A4 substrates within 9 months of the last subcutaneous dose of lenacapavir may increase the risk of adverse reactions. Alternative medications should be considered. 2. Leniolisib and Tenofovir AF: Leniolisib increases the levels or effects of tenofovir AF through other mechanisms. Alternative drugs should be used, or therapy should be modified. 3. Leniolisib and BCRP Substrates: 4. Cobicistat and Leniolisib: Cobicistat increases leniolisib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 5. Cobicistat and Letermovir: Cobicistat increases letermovir levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Tenofovir AF and Letermovir: Tenofovir AF decreases letermovir levels via P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Letermovir and P-gp Inducers: Co-administration with P-gp inducers is not recommended due to potential therapeutic failure. 8. Cobicistat and Levamlodipine: Cobicistat increases levamlodipine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. 9. Amlodipine and CYP3A Inhibitors: Monitor for hypotension and edema. 10. Cobicistat and Levoketoconazole: Cobicistat and levoketoconazole mutually increase each other's levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 11. Levoketoconazole and Elvitegravir: Levoketoconazole increases elvitegravir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Cobicistat and Levomilnacipran: Cobicistat increases levomilnacipran levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is necessary, do not exceed 80 mg of levomilnacipran daily. 13. Cobicistat and Levonorgestrel (Intrauterine): Cobicistat increases levonorgestrel levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 14. Cobicistat and Levonorgestrel (Oral): Cobicistat increases oral levonorgestrel levels, potentially raising plasma hormone concentrations. Non-hormonal contraceptives are recommended. 15. Cobicistat and Lidocaine: Cobicistat increases lidocaine levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely, especially with antiarrhythmics. 16. Cobicistat and Lomitapide: Cobicistat increases lomitapide levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of serious adverse effects. 17. Cobicistat and Lonafarnib: Cobicistat increases lonafarnib levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 18. Lonafarnib and Tenofovir AF: Lonafarnib increases tenofovir AF levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 19. Lopinavir and Elvitegravir: Lopinavir increases elvitegravir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Cobicistat and Lorlatinib: Lorlatinib decreases cobicistat levels, while cobicistat increases lorlatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. 21. Cobicistat and Losartan: Cobicistat increases losartan levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Cobicistat and Lovastatin: Cobicistat increases lovastatin levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy, including rhabdomyolysis. 23. Elvitegravir and Lovotibeglogene Autotemcel: Antiretrovirals should be discontinued at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed, as they may interfere with manufacturing. 24. Cobicistat and Lumacaftor/Ivacaftor: Cobicistat increases lumacaftor/ivacaftor levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 25. Cobicistat and Lurasidone: Cobicistat increases lurasidone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of QT prolongation. 26. Cobicistat and Methadone: Cobicistat increases methadone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. 27. Cobicistat and Midazolam: Cobicistat increases midazolam levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of prolonged sedation and respiratory depression. 28. Cobicistat and Mifepristone: Cobicistat increases mifepristone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 29. Cobicistat and Mirvetuximab Soravtansine: Cobicistat increases mirvetuximab levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Cobicistat and Modafinil: Cobicistat increases modafinil levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 31. Cobicistat and Mometasone (Inhaled): Cobicistat increases mometasone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, raising the risk of systemic corticosteroid side effects. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Cobicistat and Nafcillin: Nafcillin decreases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 33. Cobicistat and Naldemedine: Cobicistat increases naldemedine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Cobicistat and Naloxegol: Cobicistat increases naloxegol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 35. Cobicistat and Nefazodone: Cobicistat increases nefazodone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Cobicistat and Nicardipine: Cobicistat increases nicardipine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 37. Cobicistat and Nilotinib: Cobicistat increases nilotinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 38. Cobicistat and Nimodipine: Cobicistat increases nimodipine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 39. Cobicistat and Nintedanib: Cobicistat increases nintedanib levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 40. Cobicistat and Nirmatrelvir/Ritonavir: Cobicistat increases nirmatrelvir/ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Cobicistat and Nisoldipine: Cobicistat increases nisoldipine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 42. Cobicistat and Norgestrel: Cobicistat increases norgestrel levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Cobicistat and Olaparib: Cobicistat increases olaparib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 44. Cobicistat and Oliceridine: Cobicistat increases oliceridine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 45. Cobicistat and Omaveloxolone: Cobicistat increases omaveloxolone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 46. Cobicistat and Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir: Cobicistat increases ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 47. Cobicistat and Omeprazole: Cobicistat increases omeprazole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Cobicistat and Ondansetron: Cobicistat increases ondansetron levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Cobicistat and Orlistat: Orlistat decreases cobicistat levels by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Cobicistat and Osilodrostat: Cobicistat increases osilodrostat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 51. Cobicistat and Osimertinib: Cobicistat increases osimertinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 52. Cobicistat and Ospemifene: Cobicistat increases ospemifene levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Cobicistat and Otesecozole: Cobicistat increases otesecozole levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. 54. Cobicistat and Oxcarbazepine: Oxcarbazepine decreases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. This summary provides a detailed explanation of the interactions and necessary precautions for each drug combination.
